Variants.Content: The City of Divine Grace is located in the dry land of Dorne inland and connected to the Greenblood River Basin. The Dornish people valued the blessing of a perennial well, an irrigated field, or a single rainy season, and the name divine grace was derived from this life experience. The foundation of castles and settlements is not high walls, but the distribution of water sources: whoever can build canals, guard wellheads, and arrange for irrigation of fields can allow people and livestock to stay. It connects the sand and river valleys to the Sunspear road and provides rare supplies for travel.

Entry Godsgrace Local families also rely on wells, irrigation canals, orchards, drought-tolerant livestock, and travel to avoid the hot sun; if any road, well, or dock fails, the cost falls first on them.

Entry Godsgrace They also recognize Dornish accents, laws and credentials; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar or horse's hoof.

Entry Godsgrace If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Godsgrace A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Godsgrace They care about wells and springs, irrigation canals, orchards, drought-tolerant livestock, and routes to avoid the scorching sun. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
